moment.text: But a certain Samaritan, as he traveled, came where he was. When he saw him, he was moved with compassion,

previous.text: In the same way a Levite also, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.

next.text: came to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. He set him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.

payload.place: Rocky, dusty Jerusalem–Jericho road in Judea, with stony hills and scattered thorn scrub, leading toward a roadside inn
payload.timeOfDay: Midday heat, shifting to late afternoon and evening at the inn
payload.weather: Clear, dry, hot sky with no rain
payload.light: Harsh, bright sunlight on the road, softening to warm golden evening light at the inn
payload.clothing: Travelers in plain tunics and cloaks suited to dusty desert roads; the Samaritan wears a practical traveling cloak and carries oil and wine

payload.primarySubject: The Samaritan standing still on the road, gazing down at the wounded traveler.
payload.action: The Samaritan halts and looks down at the injured man lying by the roadside, his face softened with compassion.
payload.setting: Rocky, dusty Jerusalem–Jericho road in Judea, stony hills and thorn scrub stretching around.
payload.secondaryElements: The wounded traveler lies in the dust, half-clothed and bruised, his plain tunic torn. The Samaritan's donkey stands nearby, and his oil and wine jars are slung at his side.
payload.mood: Reverent, tender and compassionate, with quiet grief and human dignity.
payload.timeOfDay: Midday heat with harsh, bright sunlight on the road.
payload.composition: Medium-wide view from slightly above the roadside, the Samaritan standing and the wounded man low in the dust, the stony hills behind them.
